1) the immune system is not a passive bystander in the regulation of the stress response; 2) the effects of stress on immunity depend on the timing of stress with respect to the initiation and expression of the immunological event; and 3) stress-induced changes in immune function are mediated by a variety of neuroendocrine factors, including glucocorticoids, catecholamines and growth hormone.
